column4: ConnectToken protects file retrieval but files has no vault or individual ownership binding.
Device unregistration offers Basic or bearer authentication but ERD contains only error-response fields.
Creating an app under account_id and inferred accountId does not distinguish personal ownership from organization tenancy.
Reactor rules expose appId and projectId but the requested app-to-caller authorization relationship is unspecified.
Updating a rule requires bearer authentication but projectId and appId are unverified lookup hints.
Account-holder balance listing has authenticated access but only pagination and balanceAccounts response fields.
Document owner is inferred with no verified subject relation or lookup binding.
Legal-entity organization and individual describe entity variants rather than a proved caller authorization relationship.
UserID token management suggests user scope but security is unknown and token ERD lacks an ownership key.
Removing a user's authorization category has unknown security and only error-response columns.
Deleting a category from an authorization definition has no role evidence and only error-response fields.
Monitor resourceOwner is an inferred response field; OAuth does not establish its relation to the caller.
Workspace alert-manager definition has HMAC authentication but no tenant lookup columns.
Workspace logging configuration is authenticated but its single wrapper does not establish tenant binding.
Workspace rule-group listing has a nested path but only list and pagination fields in ERD.
Workspace retrieval lacks a verified workspace primary key or caller-tenant relation.
Event user_id is inferred and security is unknown, so an ownership lookup is unverified.
Import invalidation identifies operation_id but response uuid is not a proved lookup key and security is unknown.
Empty security permits anonymous authentication but does not prove unrestricted DAG-run note modification.
Clocking records expose project_id and user_id without verified keys or evidence choosing tenant versus individual authorization.
Company integration-setting creation is authenticated but ERD lacks a company relationship.
Company form-template listing has a tenant-like path and only pagination fields, not a verified tenant lookup.
Company integration-feature listing requires authentication but pagination fields do not establish company authorization.
Deleting a stream thumbnail requires bearer authentication; the public response flag does not authorize this mutation.
Attribute creation requires API and store keys but no explicit ownership, role or tenant policy is supplied.
Basket customer is flattened response data with ambiguous id fields rather than a proved ownership lookup.
Artifact createdBy is provenance in inferred metadata and does not establish ownership enforcement.
Artifact version metadata update has unknown security and no ownership or tenant columns.
Bill created_by occurs in flattened accounting data without a verified caller relation or database key.
Customer account and created_by are ambiguous accounting metadata rather than verified access-control relationships.
Invoice-item created_by and account fields do not establish owner-only authorization or a verified lookup.
Project API creation has unknown security and no project-to-caller binding in the inferred ERD.
Project API-version spec creation supplies descriptive fields but no verified tenant authorization relationship.
Dealer retrieval requires authentication but neither unrestricted access nor a caller ownership policy is evidenced.
Crash-count analytics includes owner_name in the path but only aggregates, leaving ownership binding unresolved.
Crash-group totals are owner-scoped by path but no owner lookup is present in the aggregate ERD.
Build detail includes owner_name in the URL but response id lacks a verified owner relationship.
Build download has owner_name context but the sole uri column cannot support an ownership lookup.
Crash-group update is token-authenticated; owner_name is only a path hint without a verified ownership relation.
App-category retrieval requires bearer authentication and supplies taxonomy relationships without an explicit authorization policy.
App-info update has app relationships but no verified caller ownership or required role evidence.
Document permissions are opaque values; JWT and Project schemes do not resolve object authorization.
Team retrieval has inferred $id but no verified primary key or caller-tenant mapping.
Team-membership creation exposes roles, userId and teamId without evidence selecting a caller role or tenant lookup.
Classification inclusion identifiers and API-key authentication do not establish a specific authorization policy.
Song-similarity lookup has unknown security and no affirmative unrestricted-access statement.
Individual electronic-address lookup has partyId and addressId but no verified party relationship or security requirements.
Registration-token or OAuth alternatives authenticate client update without specifying owner or role authorization.
Summary associates the sub-user key with an account, but response fields provide no key-to-account lookup or caller mapping.
BBC group metadata uses API-key authentication and heterogeneous fields without affirmative unrestricted-access evidence.
